kept.excerpt: The nominee resulting from this special filing and primary will be a candidate on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot. The statewide special primary is scheduled for August 11, with a special primary runoff, if necessary, on August 25. Voters who participated in the June Democratic primary are not eligible to vote in the special Republican primary.
kept.relevance: Establishes the official replacement-nomination process, election timetable, and electorate eligibility relevant to the market's resolution rules.

kept.excerpt: The Emerson College Polling/Nexstar Media survey found Ralph Norman at 22%, Darline Graham at 19%, Russell Fry at 12%, and Mark Sanford at 11%, with a quarter undecided. The survey was conducted July 28–29, 2026 among 500 likely Republican primary voters, with a margin of error of plus or minus 4.3 percentage points. Fifty-three percent said Trump's endorsement of Graham made no impact on their vote, while 29% said it made them more likely to support her and 18% less likely.
kept.relevance: Supplies a dated primary-source poll with methodology and evidence about the potential influence of Trump's endorsement.

kept.excerpt: A special Republican primary was scheduled for August 11 after Lindsey Graham, the nominee selected in the June 9 primary, died on July 11. A runoff, if needed, was scheduled for August 25. Republicans have won every South Carolina Senate election since 2004 and every gubernatorial election since 2002.
kept.relevance: Documents why a replacement primary was required and provides historical context for the importance of securing the Republican nomination.

search_notes: Evidence frozen at August 12, 2026, inclusive; no time of day was specified. Publication dates were verified from dated search-index source text, with Emerson's July 30 publication date corroborated by its publisher archive. Live 5 News was originally published August 11 and updated August 12; its displayed update timestamp is used. Excerpts are factual condensations of retrieved source text. Direct web_fetch failed because of provider configuration, and the requested agent-reach fallback returned a rate-limit error, so verification relied on web_search text rather than successfully fetched full pages. Sources dated after the cutoff, articles displaying post-cutoff updates, undated live results pages, and prediction-market or betting material were excluded. No subsequent runoff result or later development is included.
